correctness.rationale: For every n>=3,m>=2, pairs of initially white true twins cannot be forced. Once at most one white lies in each fibre, every fibre contains a blue vertex and the literal one-white-neighbour condition is exactly a cyclic triple having two full and one partial fibres. A pair of full fibres at distance <=2 initiates an adjacent full pair (if necessary filling their middle fibre), after which a maximal consecutive full run extends across the cycle; without such pair no force starts. The complement of admissible B is precisely the independence-set family of C_n squared. Ordered positive cyclic gap compositions prove its size-k count n/(n-2k) binom(n-2k,k); k=0 is 1. Edge-minimal full index sets are exactly the edges of C_n squared, giving cardinality n(m-1)+2 and count |E(C_n squared)|m^(n-2). Verified directly for 128832 starting vertex subsets in ten graph profiles against the literal color-change rule and polynomial coefficients; the unrestricted claim follows from the proof, not finite experiments.

originality.rationale: Novelty assessed only for the explicit cycle-square all-set equivalence, the closed coefficient formula and the classification of every inclusion-minimal set. The 2016 lexicographic-product paper has directly contrary Corollary 3.17 (it predicts 13 rather than the explicit 12-blue zero-forcing configuration on C5[K3]); the current proof corrects that statement, rather than claiming a number already proved there. The 2018 polynomial paper enumerates other families; 2023 well-forced paper treats trees/elementary families. The 2026 modular compression theorem covers twin-profile reduction and a generic exact exponential algorithm, but its assessed explicit specializations are star-type rather than cycle type. This broader coverage is acknowledged and limits novelty to the nontrivial closed cyclic evaluation and well-forced classification. Semantic public literature searches and published related records did not establish the exact theorem; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: A universal exact twin-profile algorithm predates the present explicit evaluation; independent expert may view cycle evaluation as a straightforward corollary.
Undiscovered papers under circular unit interval, cyclic clique expansions, true-twin substitutions or zero forcing polynomial terminology might prove the same formula.

value.rationale: The result gives a uniform closed binomial-coefficient zero forcing polynomial for every cyclic clique expansion, sharp set-level testing in terms of cyclic distance two, and a complete classification of inclusion-minimal sets and their multiplicities. It also supplies a concrete counterexample and an unbounded correction to a directly relevant published preprint scalar formula, rather than repeating a previously known bound. These address natural full enumeration and well-forcedness questions with exponentially many vertex configurations, using a structural reduction to squared-cycle independence not obtained by routine substitution into existing explicit examples. No general arbitrary-base theorem or independent certification is asserted.
